topic: Can MVDR beamforming sufficiently compensate for pattern degradation in array-fed reflectors during element failures?
consensus_response: MVDR beamforming partially compensates for pattern degradation, but its effectiveness decreases with more failed elements and is impacted by reflector surface errors and phase shifter limitations. Additional feed elements or curved arrays can alleviate gain loss, but introduce complexity and interference, affecting system capacity and reliability.
reference_context: Defocused reflector concepts show robustness against feed failures, with MVDR beamforming mitigating gain loss, but at a cost of reduced capacity and increased interference susceptibility.
